title: AI Business Systems Analyst
description:
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas – immunology, oncology, neuroscience, and eye care – and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  X ,  Facebook ,  Instagram ,  YouTube ,  LinkedIn  and  Tik Tok .
As part of AbbVie’s Business Technology Solutions (BTS), Research and Development aligned technology team, R&D Global Therapeutic Platforms is responsible for building and deploying scalable Artificial Intelligence (AI) Applications and Platforms.
The Business System Analyst will serve as an individual contributor, working directly with AI applications to support requirements gathering, development, maintenance, and enhancement. This role collaborates with data scientists, engineers, and business stakeholders to understand complex business needs and translate them into functional technology requirements. The analyst will be responsible for managing application data, monitoring system performance and accessibility, and implementing system modifications to improve productivity and efficiency.
Key duties involve eliciting, analyzing, and documenting business requirements; performing data and process modeling; and supporting change management initiatives. The analyst will also review and route system change requests, develop detailed implementation specifications, and communicate updates to management. This position requires coordinating or conducting system testing, supporting user training and educational materials, and producing reports and analysis from client databases to satisfy user requests and verify project outcomes.
The role is both consultative and technical, requiring demonstrated experience with AI technologies and tools, along with the ability to apply them to relevant business use cases. The Business System Analyst will play a critical role in supporting the evolution and continuous improvement of AI systems within the organization.
Responsibilities :
•Responsible for compliance with applicable Corporate and Divisional Policies and procedures.
•Consults with functional areas to develop understanding of the varied and complex business needs supported by the system.  Responsible for determining how changing business needs will affect the system.  Understands the role of the system in the big picture and provides ideas and recommendations regarding the evolution of the system.
•Responds to questions and influences the users regarding current and potential system inputs, processes, and outputs.  Conducts research and analysis into the nature, effect and results of system problems.  Develops detailed business user requirements, system documentation, work flow procedures, and data modeling.  Negotiates plans, time frames and trade-offs while ensuring client understands the final results of the project.
•Reviews and routes requested system changes and develops detailed specifications for implementation.  Communicates system changes and issues to next level of management.
•Ensures current and accurate system documentation, coordinates and or performs testing of system modifications, both validated and non-validated systems.  Provides systems expertise and supports system training, educational tools and materials.  Involved with the Purchasing Systems Manager regarding planning/scheduling and resource allocation.
•Produces requirements for mainframe reports, time lines, and graphics using advanced functions of a personal computer.  Creates reports from existing client databases to satisfy user requests, development of ad-hoc database reporting, data sampling, project analysis, or testing verification.
•Monitors and audits the use of the systems; executes system control practices and purchasing procedures for regulatory and compliance.
•Accountable to the purchasing customer and purchasing management for the control and administration of purchasing systems.  Systems implemented must meet projected timelines and customer expectations.  The incumbent supports various mainframe, Lotus Notes, stand-alone applications, divisional interfaced systems that impact the overall purchasing process.
•Bachelor's Degree and 2 years experience or Master's Degree in Information Systems or related field is required.
•Experience in the systems development, implementation, and operations of a large-scale, enterprise systems.
•Experience with Artificial Intelligence, Large Language Models, and their capabilities
•Excellent interpersonal skills and well-developed verbal and written communication skills.
•Must be able to effectively lead and facilitate meetings with customers and technical team members.
•Must be deliverables focused and detail oriented.
•Must exhibit exceptional teamwork skills.
•Must have a strong customer focus.

description:

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. Purpose
Describe the primary goals, objectives or functions or outputs of this position.
This is a field-based role covering Michigan,
The Account Specialist role promotes a product to community practices and health systems. Customer accounts may include community/private practices, community-based hospitals, academic medical centers, and government accounts (military treatment facilities and/or Veteran’s Affairs Medical Centers). The Account Specialist develops and maintains relationships with various accounts/departments such as neurology, pain medicine, physical medicine and rehabilitation, primary care, and pharmacy. Or in Urology, specialists such as urology, urogynecology, obstetrics and gynecology, female pelvic medicine, ambulatory surgical centers, and reconstructive surgery.

Promote a product to meet/exceed sales goals in community/private practices as well as hospitals/health systems.
Identify/uncover customer needs (training, clinical, operational, reimbursement) and address with appropriate AbbVie resources
Provide education and clinical/injection training for residents, fellows, and other key hospital personnel.
Expert delivery of anatomical/procedural information and training, including the appropriate use of anatomical terminology to train injection paradigms/postures while highlighting various anatomical and injection insights and considerations.
Effectively utilize AbbVie's sales and data resources to enhance productivity and growth of AbbVie products while implementing U.S. Marketing Plan.
Collaborate with other Account Specialist to promote the product for approved indications and execute individual, department, or group resident/fellow trainings within hospital/health system accounts.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in health, sciences, pharmacy or business-related field preferred or relevant and equivalent industry experience required.
Relevant and equivalent industry experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree is at least five (5) years of technical experience with three (3) or more years of experience within sales preferred and a high school diploma/GED required
Experience with Buy & Bill and/or Specialty Pharmacy products is preferred, in both health systems and private practice
Ability to lift/pull 25–100 lb. training models and meet necessary hospital credentialing/vaccination requirements
Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements
Ability to travel adequately to cover territory, as well as overnight attendance at scheduled training events and sales meetings
Documented history of strong sales performance, preferably in a clinical/technical/consultative sales role with multiple decision makers is preferred. Ability to manage a complex sell, learn procedural, technical, clinical, and anatomical information quickly and communicate/present/train to a variety of audiences
An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials.
These HCIR credentialing requirements may include, but are not limited to, background checks, drug screens, proof of immunization/vaccination for various diseases, fingerprinting and specific licenses required by individual state or cities. Please remember that you are solely responsible for ensuring that you satisfy all HCIR credentialing requirements and for any associated liability for failing to do so. The Associate Director, Statistics provides statistical leadership for clinical development and life-cycle management strategies for assigned projects. Specific areas of work may include clinical trials, patient safety, and global medical affairs. The Associate Director works in partnership with experts in multiple disciplines to advance medicines to our patients.
Responsibilities:
Provide expertise/lead regulatory submission and product life-cycle management strategy planning and implementation for assigned projects. Represent function/department on project team(s) to provide statistical input to compound/drug development and drive alignment with functional management. Partner with other functions (Clinical, Regulatory, Patient Safety, or GMA) to create development strategies for assigned projects.

Develop strategy for data presentation and inference. Ensure appropriate interpretation of statistical deliverables in collaboration with other functions. Collaborate in publication of scientific research. Ensure accuracy and internal consistency of reports and publications, including tables, listings, and figures.
Act as the liaison for statistical issues on AbbVie collaborative studies with CROs, academic institutions, government agencies, steering and/or data monitoring committees, joint ventures or licensing collaborators. Build external scientific connections which foster professional development and promote the reputation of the Statistics department.

Minimum Qualifications:
MS (with 10+ years of experience) or PhD (with 6+ years of experience) in Statistics, Biostatistics, or a highly related field.
Have strong leadership skills and experience in working/managing cross-cultural or oversea teams
Pharmaceutical or related industry knowledge required, including experience and understanding of drug development and life-cycle management in the regulated environment.
Preferred Qualifications:
PhD preferred
Submission experience preferred
Other Required Skills:
High degree of technical competence and excellent communication skills, both oral and written
Able to identify data or analytical issues, and assist with providing solutions by either applying own skills and knowledge or seeking help from others

title: Associate Director, Business Excellence Portfolio Strategy Aesthetics
description:
At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit https://global.allerganaesthetics.com/. Follow Allergan Aesthetics on LinkedIn.
The Business Excellence Strategy group within Global Portfolio Strategy & Operations works side-by-side with the Aesthetics R&D executive team on many of the most pressing issues facing the organization, both in the short- and long-term. Work from this team will have a direct impact on the future success of AbbVie.
As an Associate Director of Business Excellence Portfolio Strategy, you will partner with leaders across AbbVie to optimize the value of our portfolio and current/future assets. The role is seeking a high performing team member who has demonstrated an interest and expertise in the biopharma industry and strong desire to advance our strategic agenda and support mission-critical assets + initiatives that will make a real difference for AbbVie’s patients. In return, the Business Excellence group will provide high profile, high impact projects and professional development experiences spanning the entire drug development value chain.
The position requires strong analytical skills and the ability to translate strategic vision into tactical action. It will be imperative in this role to identify the highest impact ideas and plans and focus efforts to work effectively in a cross-functional team.
This position is located in our Irvine, CA office (hybrid onsite days at Tues, Wed and Thurs).
Responsibilities:
•    Drive end-to-end strategic innovation, communication and execution on Allergan Aesthetics portfolio + assets in partnership with the R&D + Commercial Leadership Teams. Areas of focus include strategic planning, scenario evaluation, and data-driven problem solving spanning the breadth of drug/aesthetic medical device development.
•    Support R&D strategy processes including: Annual franchise strategy reviews and Strategy Long Range Plans, Therapeutic Area strategy and pipeline reviews, and high priority Asset Strategy Team support. This will require both strong project management and ability to generate and communicate strategic insights to leaders and franchise / asset strategy teams.
•    Support and lead strategic initiatives that address mission-critical questions and position AbbVie for future success, such as:

description:
About AbbVie

The Biologics CMC Development team at AbbVie in the Bay Area has a long and rich history of biologics development. Now located in a new state of the art facility in South San Francisco, the team leverages its comprehensive end-to-end CMC capabilities to work collaboratively through all phases of CMC development with a primary focus on advancing complex biologic therapies, such as bi-specifics and novel modalities, to human clinical studies and eventual licensure. This role is within a team of highly experienced scientists and managers who have directly enabled the development/IND submissions of 20+ novel oncology drugs and successfully filed two BLAs.
As one of CMC purification development associate scientists, you will work in the CMC purification team to develop robust, phase-appropriate processes for drug substance GMP production to enable human clinical studies and eventual licensure. This position is an onsite role in a lab-based function. To be successful, candidates must enjoy and thrive in an onsite, highly collaborative lab environment with daily face-to-face interactions between scientists.
Responsibilities:
Support development, optimization, and scale-up of purification processes through lab-based and -scale up lab operation activities
Support transfer of purification processes to GMP manufacturing for clinical material production
Execute routine purification development operations from harvest to UF/DF following established protocols, independently after appropriate training, and generate reliable and consistent results
Analyze and critique experimental results, document and promptly communicate significant deviations or unexpected results
Prepare small to large (500L) batches of buffer solutions following batch record recipe
Support scale up lab activities including preparation and execution
Perform routine analytical measurements using HPLC and UV-vis instrumentation
Accurately record experimental observations and results at the time of execution; maintain complete, traceable data sets and batch records, including instrument files and analytical results, in electronic notebooks, databases, and Excel files in accordance with established documentation procedures and timelines
Perform general lab maintenance including cleanliness, equipment maintenance and maintaining inventory

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. The Biologics CMC Development team at AbbVie in the Bay Area has a long and rich history of biologics development. Now located in a new state of the art facility in South San Francisco, the team leverages its comprehensive end-to-end CMC capabilities to work collaboratively through all phases of CMC development with a primary focus on advancing complex biologic therapies, such as bi-specifics and novel modalities, to human clinical studies and eventual licensure. This Scientist I role is within a team of highly experienced scientists and managers who have directly enabled the development/IND submissions of 20+ novel oncology drugs and successfully filed two BLAs.
As a CMC purification development scientist, you will independently design, execute, and interpret experiments to develop robust, phase-appropriate purification processes for drug substance GMP production to enable human clinical studies and eventual licensure. This position is an onsite, lab-based role requiring close collaboration and daily face-to-face interactions with scientists.
Responsibilities:
Develop, optimize, and scale up purification processes for monoclonal antibodies, multi-specifics, antibody-like molecules, and other complex biologic candidates across early- and late-stage drug substance process development; independently design and execute experiments, interpret results, and recommend next steps.
Support transfer of purification processes to GMP manufacturing sites for clinical material production, including preparation of technical documentation.
Evaluate novel, advanced bioprocess technologies that are in line with the group’s strategy
Plan and execute laboratory and scale-up activities efficiently, collaborating within the team and cross-functionally to meet project timelines and goals.
Work with contract laboratories to plan and execute assigned viral clearance studies, interpret results, and contribute to technical documentation.
Author technical reports and maintain complete, traceable experimental and batch records, including instrument and analytical data, in approved electronic systems; document results at execution and follow established procedures and timelines.
Prepare and deliver technical presentations and group-meeting updates; critically evaluate experimental results, communicate recommendations, and promptly document and communicate significant deviations or unexpected results
Follow applicable laboratory and scale-up facility safety procedures and standard operating procedures (SOPs), complete required training before performing assigned activities, and contribute to laboratory readiness through equipment maintenance, cleanliness, and inventory management
Bachelor’s degree with 5+ years of relevant industry experience or Master’s degree with typically 2+ years of relevant industry experience (in Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry, Chemistry, or a closely related field, preferred)
Must have protein purification experience including chromatography separations and filtration operations
Excellent attention to detail; ability to follow written experimental protocols and safety procedures and maintain accurate, complete, and traceable written records
Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to answer scientific questions, troubleshoot purification operations, and recommend next steps
Demonstrated ability to learn, understand and master new experimental techniques
Able to work collaboratively within and outside of the group
Able to author technical reports and presentations
Has understanding of biochemistry and bioprocess engineering concepts
Strong planning and analytical skills, including the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and identify, document, and communicate significant deviations or unexpected results
Experience with AKTA chromatographic instruments (such as AKTA Avant, AKTA Purifier, AKTA Pure or similar)
Demonstrated scientific writing skills and strong verbal communication skills including scientific data presentations
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn new software applications for experimental documentation, data analysis, and reporting
Preferred:
Has hands on experience with executing antibody or antibody-like molecule purification techniques including resin chromatography (affinity, CEX, AEX, MMC), depth filtration, virus filtration, membrane chromatography, and TFF operations.
Has hands on experience with monoclonal antibody or antibody-like molecule purification at GMP, pilot and/or laboratory scale
Understanding of analytical techniques, such as HPLC, LAL, and ELISA
Has hands on experience with high-throughput technologies and automation

This position will require strong enterprise leadership to navigate the organization through multiple external environment pressures on global pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement.
This role bridges early asset development and future commercialization readiness, ensuring that pricing and access considerations are embedded from the earliest stages of the drug development lifecycle and through Phase 3 design and identification of evidence needs. The Senior Director serves as the definitive voice of pipeline market access, shaping clinical trial design, evidence generation, and target product profiles through a global access and reimbursement lens.  Importantly this position will need to define distinct US and international strategies to optimize global launch success.
The Senior Director will lead a team of experts across both US Pipeline Strategy and International Pipeline Strategy and will have an opportunity to define the objectives and vision for the team appropriately.  This role will provide leadership across both domestic and global dimensions of pipeline access, partnering deeply with inline US and International access teams as well as R&D, Regulatory, HEOR, Global Commercial Development, Business Development, and Government Affairs to deliver integrated access strategies that position AbbVie's pipeline for long-term commercial and patient-access success.
Key Responsibilities
Pipeline Access Strategy & Portfolio Leadership
Owns the end-to-end pipeline Integrated access strategy for all pre-launch and development-stage assets within the assigned Business Unit, ensuring strategies are comprehensive in addressing evidence needs, policy considerations, pricing potential, and commercial considerations. IASs integrate global needs and dynamics through regulatory submission.
Serves as the primary voice of pipeline market access strategies at Business Unit governance forums, including LMG, TASC, CSM,  ASTs , and other senior leadership reviews — communicating access risk, opportunity, and strategic direction with clarity and conviction.
Serves as the voice of access into pipeline Business Development opportunities.
Leads prioritization exercises across the pipeline portfolio to ensure resources and strategic attention are allocated to assets with the greatest near- and long-term access complexity and business impact.
Creates and optimizes launch strategies inclusive of considerations for IRA, MFN, and other market forces (US Channel dynamics) to position the asset for sequencing strategies across indications as well as geographies incorporating the pressures
Defines and delivers the Access Roadmap— a cross-functionally developed strategy that articulates the access approach for each pipeline asset by development phase, anticipated launch timing, and global evidence deliverables.
Early Development Integration
Partners with R&D and Regulatory teams to embed access-relevant endpoints, comparators, and trial design elements into clinical development programs from Phase I/II onward — ensuring studies are powered to meet payer and HTA evidence standards at launch and partners with the affiliates.
Defines and champions Target Product Profiles (TPPs) from a market access perspective, translating payer value requirements into actionable clinical and evidence generation guidance for asset teams.
Generates and maintains global payer and HTA evidence requirements across major markets (US, EU5, Japan, and emerging markets), ensuring development programs proactively address the evidence gaps that govern access and reimbursement decisions.
US & International Strategy Alignment
Provides strategic leadership and direction to the US Pipeline Strategy Lead and International Pipeline Strategy Lead, ensuring both domestic and global perspectives are fully integrated into a cohesive, Business Unit-level pipeline access strategy.
Aligns US payer strategy, formulary positioning, and value communication frameworks with international HTA, pricing, and reimbursement approaches — creating a globally consistent access narrative that can flex to local market requirements.
Anticipates cross-market reference pricing dynamics, parallel trade risks, and HTA precedent effects, incorporating these considerations into early pipeline access strategy to protect long-term portfolio value across geographies.
Partners closely with US and International Pipeline Strategy Leads to develop and execute a structured pipeline-to-launch transition framework, ensuring that market access strategies, payer evidence packages, and reimbursement submissions are fully prepared ahead of regulatory approval.
Collaborates with US and international commercial, medical, and market access teams to ensure seamless knowledge transfer and strategic handoff at the point of regulatory approval — including payer communication plans, launch sequencing strategies, and country-level access readiness assessments.
Leads cross-functional launch readiness reviews in partnership with US and International teams to identify and resolve access gaps (evidence, pricing approvals, formulary positioning) prior to approval, ensuring no delays to patient access at launch.
Ensures that affiliate and in-country market access teams are equipped with globally aligned value messages, health economic tools, and reimbursement dossiers well in advance of launch — bridging the transition from pipeline to commercial ownership.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Partnership
Provides strategic direction and partnership to cross-functional groups including HEOR, R&D, Regulatory, Global Commercial Development, Global Marketing, Government Affairs, and Business Development — ensuring market access perspectives are fully integrated into all pipeline asset decisions.
Leads the development of Integrated Evidence Plans (IEPs) in close collaboration with HEOR, ensuring real-world evidence, health economic modeling, and outcomes research strategies are aligned with anticipated payer and HTA requirements at launch.
Partners with Government Affairs to anticipate and shape the evolving policy and reimbursement landscape, embedding policy risk and opportunity assessments into pipeline access strategies.
Collaborates with Global Commercial Development and Global Marketing to ensure pipeline access strategies are aligned with brand positioning, indication sequencing, and long-range commercial forecasts.
Business Development & Asset Evaluation
Works closely with Business Development to inform the market access potential of in-licensing, partnership, and acquisition opportunities — providing rigorous payer landscape assessments, reimbursement probability analyses, and access risk evaluations to support BD decision-making.
Establishes and communicates access-based licensing priorities, ensuring that pipeline expansion decisions account for payer value evidence requirements, competitive access dynamics, and global pricing sustainability.
Serves as the access subject matter expert in due diligence processes, assessing the payer readiness and evidence maturity of externally sourced pipeline assets being evaluated for AbbVie's portfolio.
Governance, Stakeholder Engagement & People Leadership
Represents pipeline market access priorities at senior leadership governance forums, portfolio review committees, and cross-Business Unit strategy sessions — serving as the definitive voice on access considerations that should inform pipeline investment and development decisions.
Builds, develops, and retains a high-performing pipeline access team, providing mentorship, career development, and performance management for direct and indirect reports across US and international functions.
Fosters a culture of innovation, rigor, and affiliate-centricity within the pipeline access team — ensuring that affiliate launch needs, in-country market dynamics, and local payer requirements are actively incorporated into global strategy development.
Education
An advanced degree (MBA, MPH, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent) in business, health economics, public policy, life sciences, or a related field is required.
Formal training or demonstrated expertise in health technology assessment (HTA), health economics, outcomes research, or pharmaceutical development is strongly preferred.
Bachelor's degree in a scientific, business, or public health discipline is required as a minimum baseline.
Experience
A minimum of 12–15 years of progressive, senior-level experience in market access, pricing, reimbursement, HEOR, or a closely related pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical function — with a substantial portion of that experience focused on pipeline and pre-launch strategy.
Demonstrated expertise in global market access, including a deep working knowledge of HTA processes, payer evidence requirements, pricing and reimbursement frameworks, and access decision-making dynamics across major international markets (US, EU5, Japan, and additional key markets).
Proven experience shaping clinical development strategy from a market access and outcomes evidence perspective — including direct experience contributing to clinical trial design, endpoint selection, and Integrated Evidence Plan development in collaboration with R&D teams.
Strong track record of leading and developing high-performing teams in a matrixed, multinational environment, with demonstrated ability to manage direct reports and influence cross-functional partners without direct authority.
Experience supporting Business Development activities including asset due diligence, licensing evaluations, and access-based valuation assessments is highly preferred.
Comfortable operating at the senior leadership level, with demonstrated ability to communicate complex access strategy to executive audiences and influence enterprise-level pipeline investment decisions.
Experience across multiple therapeutic areas (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Neuroscience) is an asset, though deep expertise in at least one is required.

Strategic Vision & Access Leadership
Global HTA & Payer Expertise
Clinical Development Partnership
Evidence Generation Strategy
Cross-Functional Influence
Pipeline Portfolio Prioritization
Business Development Acumen

People Leadership & Talent Development

title: Engineering Manager, Marketing Technology
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
THE COMMUNITY YOU WILL JOIN
Airbnb's Marketing Technology organization builds the infrastructure that powers how we reach and connect with guests and hosts around the world — from audience segmentation and campaign orchestration to last-mile delivery and real-time insights. Our engineers work at the intersection of scale, reliability, and product impact, building platforms that carry billions of messages each year across email, SMS, push, and WhatsApp. We are deeply committed to building AI-natively: agents and LLM-powered automation are becoming core to how we build, operate, and improve our systems.
You'll lead two closely partnered teams that together own Airbnb's communications platform end to end. The Orchestration team builds the systems that let marketing and product teams design and run personalized, event- and list-triggered customer journeys at Airbnb scale. The Delivery team owns the last mile — routing every notification through the right provider, tracking it to a terminal state, and managing contact preferences and vendor relationships. Both teams collaborate deeply with audience segmentation, content, ML, and data engineering teams, as well as product partners across the company.
THE DIFFERENCE YOU WILL MAKE
As the Engineering Manager for this team, you will be the primary technical leader for the systems that decide whether a message reaches a guest or host — and when. You'll set the technical direction, own roadmap execution, and build the kind of team culture where engineers grow and do the best work of their careers, including through deep, genuine adoption of AI-native engineering practices.
The platform is mid-transformation. We are consolidating legacy and next-generation messaging flows onto a single unified path, moving platform health from component metrics to business-impact signals such as campaign delivery SLAs and burn rate, and building end-to-end observability so any owner — human or agent — can answer "what happened to notification X for user Y" in minutes. At the same time, both teams are standing up agentic capabilities: an agent-driven orchestration layer, end-to-end lifecycle testing agents, smart notification scheduling, and AI-assisted on-call triage. You will be the leader who ensures these systems ship with the rigor, reliability, and operational maturity that production-grade messaging and agentic systems demand.
Your leadership will directly determine how reliably Airbnb communicates with its community, how confidently partner teams can build on the platform, and how effectively this team leads Marketing Technology's shift toward AI-native engineering.
A TYPICAL DAY
Lead planning, roadmap reviews, and cross-team syncs for Delivery and Orchestration, keeping delivery on track and stakeholders well-informed
Run 1:1s with engineers across both teams, with intentional focus on career growth, technical skill development, and early identification of blockers
Serve as the primary engineering point of contact for cross-team dependencies — fielding requests from product teams across Airbnb and making clear, reasoned prioritization calls
Partner with the Product Manager to sequence the roadmap across journey orchestration, bulk campaign sends, and delivery infrastructure
Drive technical strategy for end-to-end observability and SLA-driven delivery: campaign-level delivery tracking, health-gated ramping, dynamic pacing against budgets, and automatic provider failover
Oversee the design, delivery, and operational health of production agentic systems: agent-driven orchestration, lifecycle testing agents, smart scheduling, and LLM-assisted on-call triage
Champion AI-native development practices across both teams — from AI-assisted coding and review to agents in CI/CD, on-call response, and delivery anomaly detection
Own the health and operational maturity of both teams: daytime and 24/7 on-call programs, blameless incident retrospectives, SLO definitions, runbook quality, and third-party messaging vendor escalations
Represent the communications platform in org-wide planning cycles and contribute to the broader Marketing Technology engineering strategy
YOUR EXPERTISE

title: Principal Product Manager, Global from Day 1, International Seller Services
description:
Amazon's Worldwide Global Selling team builds the products and programs that help sellers grow their business across Amazon's global marketplace network. Global from Day 1 (GfD) lets sellers reach customers in new marketplaces from their first listing, without first committing inventory, capital, or per-country setup. China-based sellers already offer US customers millions of products. Much of that selection ships from China with delivery times and reliability that fall short of what US customers expect, and much more selection never reaches Amazon at all.
We are seeking a Principal Product Manager to own GfD growth for China-based sellers in the US. You will have two goals. The first is to improve the delivery experience for selection that sellers in China currently fulfill. The second is to use GfD to bring selection that is new to Amazon into the US store. This is a single-threaded ownership role with VP-level visibility. You will define the multi-year vision, own the inputs that drive selection and delivery-speed outcomes, and align supply chain, fulfillment, catalog, compliance, and seller recruitment teams on one roadmap.
The ideal candidate thinks in systems, reasons from data, and leads through influence across large, matrixed organizations. They are comfortable owning a P&L-relevant program where customer delivery promise, seller economics, and Amazon's fulfillment capacity all have to be traded off explicitly.
Key job responsibilities
- Define and own the 3 to 5 year GfD vision and roadmap for China-based sellers in the US, setting clear targets for delivery speed, delivery reliability, and new-to-Amazon selection.
- Improve the delivery experience for selection that sellers in China fulfill today. You will benchmark delivery days, cost, and reliability for each channel against US FBA, MFN shipped from China, and competitors, then close the gaps through GfD fulfillment options.
- Drive the creation of selection that is new to Amazon. You will work out which product categories and seller segments GfD can bring to US customers, then partner with seller recruitment and account management to grow that selection.
- Define the path from GfD to in-country FBA so that sellers can graduate once demand is proven. GfD selection should add to the FBA business and lead sellers into it, not compete with it.
- Partner with FBA, Cross-Border Fulfillment, Global Logistics, Catalog, Global Compliance, Pricing, Ads, Finance, and the China seller services teams to align roadmaps and resolve gaps that no single team owns.

- Write strategic documents (6-pagers, PR/FAQs, OP1/OP2 inputs) that align senior stakeholders and secure investment.
- Represent GfD for China sellers in the US in WBRs, MBRs, QBRs, and VP-level reviews as the single accountable owner.
- Mentor product and program managers across the GfD workstreams, and raise the bar on customer-backed and data-driven decisions.

title: Principal Product Manager, Technical ES, Mission AI
description:
Some of the most consequential AI work in the country happens where the internet does not reach. As the Principal Product Manager for Mission AI, you will decide what that work becomes. You will own the product strategy for AI capability delivered on one of the largest AI infrastructure programs AWS has ever taken on: a dedicated, accredited GPU environment where strong open-weight and Amazon models are adapted to a national security customer's own data and problems.
There is no established product playbook for this. Public benchmarks, model hubs, and package repositories are not available inside the environment, compute is a fixed on-premises fleet, and the customer's mission needs are still being defined. You will work directly with the customer's technical leaders, analysts, and operators to find the problems worth solving, then turn them into clear requirements that scientists and engineers can build against. You will decide what ships first, what "better than the base model" has to mean before we claim it, and how capability moves from the lab to the people who rely on it. You will also set product direction for the program's infrastructure product manager, so platform and AI capability run as one roadmap.
You join at the start. The lab's first scientists are being hired now, and the decisions you make in your first year shape both what the program delivers and what it is asked to deliver next.
The candidate selected must obtain and maintain a security clearance at the TS/SCI with polygraph level. Upon start, the selected candidate will be sponsored for a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the product vision and multi-year roadmap for mission AI capability: adapted models, evaluation suites, and the inference and agentic services the customer's engineers integrate into their mission systems.
- Run discovery with customer technical leads, analysts, and operators to find and rank the highest-value mission use cases, and write the narratives (PR/FAQ, strategy documents) that drive investment decisions.
- Define what success means for each use case before work starts, partnering with the lab's science leads to set evaluation standards and the margin a model must clear to count as an improvement.
- Translate mission needs into functional and technical requirements, and make the trade-offs between capability, compute budget, schedule, and accreditation constraints.
- Own launch readiness inside the accredited environment: technical readiness, independent verification and validation, accreditation and authorization gates, operational handoff, and customer adoption.
- Shape future task orders: build the evidence-backed business case and scope for the next wave of mission AI work, partnering with program, contracts, and finance.
- Be accountable for outcomes: track adoption, mission impact, and delivery against goals, and report progress in program and executive reviews.
- Own customer engagement across the service lifecycle: adoption, optimization, problem resolution, and evolution of each capability once it is in mission use. Own escalations on the services you ship and dive deep with engineers to resolve them.
- Influence the engineering roadmaps of the customer's technical decision makers, so their mission systems are built to take advantage of what the lab delivers next.
- Write architecture and technical requirements documents for the lab's services, and contribute to engineering design reviews on how they are built, served, and scaled.
- Partner with Tech Business Development, Solutions Architects, ProServe, and engineering leaders inside and outside AWS to drive service success.
- Set product direction for and mentor the program's infrastructure product manager, and help hire and develop the product team as the program scales.
A day in the life
You start the morning reading the overnight evaluation results with the lab's scientists, checking whether an adapted model has cleared the bar you agreed with the customer for a priority mission task. Mid-morning, you work with customer analysts on a workflow they run every day, looking for the step where a model would change their outcome rather than just their speed. After lunch, you review the infrastructure team's serving plan and decide whether the next release can meet its accreditation gate on schedule or needs to be re-scoped. You close the day drafting the business case for a capability the customer has not asked for yet, but that the evidence says they will need in the next task order.
About the team
The Mission AI Model Lab is the science team behind AWS's Mission AI program. We take existing models and make them useful for problems that matter to national security, working on dedicated AI infrastructure built for exactly that. This lab is purpose-built and these are among its first scientists, so the people who join now help shape how it works and what it builds. We sit where frontier-model research meets national security delivery, and we value invention on genuinely new problems, evaluation we can defend, and plain talk with the people who rely on what we build.
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

title: Principal TPM, AI Engineering, AI Engineering
description:
Software engineering is where AI is changing work fastest. Developers everywhere now use AI coding tools, but the organizational gains have not followed, and most enterprises have faster individual developers alongside the same delivery outcomes. AWS AI Engineering exists to close that gap. We help customers systematically build better software with AI across the whole software development lifecycle. AI-native development is now moving from early adopters into the enterprise, and the hard part is no longer proving that it works. It is making it scale.
We are looking for a Principal TPM to help shape how that happens. You will work alongside our engineering teams to bring direction together from two streams of signal: what we learn inside customers' engineering organizations, and where the industry is heading. Customer signal tells you what hurts today. Industry signal tells you what will be table stakes in six months. Connecting the two into a point of view the team can act on, and keeping it current as both move, is the center of this role.
Our current work includes an open-source, AI-native development lifecycle we created and continue to evolve with customers, along with offerings that give AI agents a deep understanding of large codebases and move customers toward autonomous software delivery. Those offerings will keep changing as the technology does, and the charter behind them will not.
Key job responsibilities
Bring the direction together
Work with our engineering teams to connect customer signal and industry signal into a clear direction for how AWS helps customers become AI-native across the software development lifecycle. Find where teams are solving the same problem in parallel and bring that work together, so the organization makes one piece of real progress rather than three partial ones. Help sequence work against customer readiness and keep the portfolio coherent as individual offerings come and go.
Define the methodology, then make it adoptable
Drive the definition, standardization, and adoption of our AI-native development lifecycle as something customers can run themselves. Build consensus on the practices and standards that make it real, and replace fragmented experimentation with a credible default path that fits each customer's risk tolerance.
Own adoption, and scale it
Treat adoption as the deliverable rather than the follow-up, through enablement, documentation, reference implementations, assessments, and self-service paths that carry customers from first experiment to production-scale practice. Design the mechanisms that convert individual developer adoption into enterprise standardization and that let the wider AWS field carry this work without you in the room. Account for organizations whose constraints differ from the ones you designed for, and for the long tail where adoption usually stalls.
Define how success is measured, and hold us to it
Define and track outcome-based KPIs for the charter, including adoption and depth of use inside customer organizations, persistence of changed behavior long after the engagement, and improvements in delivery speed, quality, and the economics of building software. Insist on rigorous evaluation of the offerings we build, the agents inside them, and our own claims about what works. Build measurement frameworks customers can run on themselves, and recommend stopping work that is not paying off.
Build leverage out of engagements
Turn lessons from individual customer engagements into repeatable patterns and scalable assets. Productize what was built for one customer when it has broader value, and resist treating every new request as bespoke. Represent the voice of the customer internally, translating patterns and adoption blockers into actionable input for AWS service teams so that what we learn in the field shapes the products customers build on.
Lead across the organization and with customers
Influence without relying on authority, aligning engineering, field, and regional teams worldwide on shared direction and sequencing. Act as a trusted advisor to customer executives and practitioners, solving the business problem rather than only the technical one and investing in the long-term relationship over the one-off win. Build the playbook and enablement that lets the wider AWS field carry this work, and represent it externally through open source, conference talks, and technical writing.
A day in the life
You split your time between setting direction and staying close to the work. On one day you might sit with a customer's engineering team to understand why they abandoned part of the lifecycle after week three, then meet a CTO to agree what success looks like for a 15,000 developer organization. On another you might review adoption data across regions to decide where the next investment goes, work out what a stalled rollout actually needs, or turn a pattern that worked for one customer into something the whole field can run. You make calls with incomplete information, hold direction under pressure, and change course when the evidence warrants.

The decisions you make, about what we build, how we package it, who we build it for, and how we bring it to market, will define how businesses buy, sell, and operate in the age of AI. • Drive delivery in ambiguous, novel problem spaces where methodological and business strategy has not yet been defined, creating structure and a path forward where none exists.
Science-Systems Technical Judgment

Process Improvement & Automation
• Identify and drive automation and process improvement across measurement-science delivery — reducing manual overhead and recurring effort while preserving data integrity.

After lunch, you could be driving a program review that aligns three teams on a shared delivery plan, surfacing a methodological risk that needs science leadership’s decision. Later, you present a program narrative to a VP, distilling a significantly complex cross-team effort into a clear, data-driven recommendation. You end the day mentoring a TPM on the team. title: Sr. Product Manager - Tech, OpsTech Solutions, OTS Delivery Software Engineering (DSE)
description:
Every Amazon package that ships, every grocery order that is fulfilled, and every associate who needs IT help depends on technology our teams keep running. Amazon's OpsTech Solutions (OTS) is the IT operations and infrastructure organization for all of Amazon Worldwide Operations, including Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS), delivering reliable technology to more than one million associates and operators across every geography. OTS is transforming from reactive support to proactive, prescriptive, AI-powered service delivery, and ServiceNow is the platform where that work happens.
What this role is: You will own the product strategy for the OTS Incident Management Platform (ITSM), the core system of record and orchestration layer for how the organization receives, records, routes, and resolves work. Every requester contact, Service Desk interaction, and Field IT task flows through the incident record you own. You decide what gets built, what gets retired, and how ITSM becomes the foundation that the rest of the OTS product portfolio plugs into.
Our team is organized around three questions that apply to every persona we serve: How does someone ask for help? How does the organization receive and organize that work? How does the work get resolved? This role owns the center of that model. Your peers own the requester front door (OneSupportHub and Virtual Agent), Service Desk Workforce Optimization, AI resolution intelligence (OTS Assist and PathFinder), and Field IT productivity. ITSM is where all of those come together on a single record, so the decisions you make shape how well every adjacent product works.
The opportunity is to move ITSM from a place where fulfillers log work to a platform that actively guides it. Today, Service Desk fulfillers and Field IT technicians lose time to platform friction and assemble each resolution themselves from memory and scattered knowledge. You will turn ITSM into the orchestrator that brings AI-generated resolution plans, validated data, and trusted knowledge into the fulfiller's workflow, so the right next step is the obvious one. Your customers are Service Desk fulfillers, Field IT technicians and managers, knowledge authors, and the engineers who integrate other services with the incident record.
Key Highlights
• Own the product strategy and roadmap for the OTS Incident Management Platform (ITSM), the system of record and orchestration layer for OTS work.
• Drive the reactive-to-prescriptive transformation by making ITSM the place where AI-generated resolution plans become the default way to work an incident.
• Lead Knowledge Base improvements so content is easy to find, trustworthy, and measured.
• Work at the center of a product team whose adjacent products (intake, routing, workforce optimization, AI resolution) all depend on your platform.
Key job responsibilities
- Define and own a multi-year product vision and roadmap for ITSM, covering incident and task management, orchestration and validation, ITSM user experience, and Knowledge Management.
- Act as the voice of the customer for Service Desk and Field IT, using shadowing, feedback, and operational data to translate real workflow friction into prioritized requirements.
- Partner with the AI resolution product team to deliver prescriptive, guided resolution on the incident record, and own the fulfiller-facing experience and its adoption.
- Set clear ownership boundaries and integration contracts between ITSM and adjacent products (intake, routing, workforce optimization, AI agents) so teams build on the platform rather than around it.
- Partner with engineering leaders to shape platform architecture, drive build-vs-configure-vs-buy decisions on ServiceNow, and manage platform health and technical debt.
- Establish north-star and adoption metrics for the platform (e.g., handle time, resolution-plan adoption, documentation quality, knowledge reuse) and report on them through Monthly and Quarterly Business Reviews.
- Contribute to annual planning mechanisms (OP1/OP2) with clear, well-reasoned investment proposals, and maintain mechanisms to continuously capture voice of the customer.
A day in the life
Your day moves between the floor and the roadmap. You might start by shadowing IT technicians to see where a knowledge article pulls them off a ticket or where a chat times out mid-conversation, then turn those observations into user stories with your engineering partners. Midday, you join an architecture discussion on how AI-generated resolution plans write back to the incident record and where that boundary sits with the AI team. In the afternoon, you review adoption metrics, make prioritization trade-offs with stakeholders across the IT organization, and draft a strategy narrative or OP2 investment proposal for senior review.
About the team
The ServiceNow Product Management team builds the products that are the backbone of OTS operations. Amazon employees, Service Desk agents, and Field IT technicians rely on these ServiceNow experiences to complete their work every day. The team is a group of Product Managers, each owning one clear product space so they can go deep instead of switching between unrelated problems, supported by a dedicated UX designer. Your engineering counterparts sit within the same larger organization, and your primary stakeholders are the Service Desk and Field IT organizations.

title: AI Research Scientist: Multimodal Foundation Models - Architecture, Pre-Training & Distillation
description:
The Multimodal Intelligence Team is building the next generation of foundation models for Apple experiences. We are looking for a research scientist to advance the architectures, pre-training methods, and distillation techniques that make highly capable multimodal models practical across the Apple ecosystem.
Our research spans the full foundation-model lifecycle: model architecture, pre-training objectives, data mixtures, optimization, scaling, distillation, and evaluation. A defining challenge of our work is to develop models that combine broad intelligence with the memory, latency, energy, and privacy requirements of on-device deployment.
You will have the opportunity to shape new research directions, conduct ambitious experiments at scale, and translate successful ideas into foundation-model technologies that can reach Apple products. Where appropriate, this work may also lead to publications and the open sourcing of selected models, research artifacts, evaluations, or tools.
In this role, you will investigate fundamental questions about how multimodal foundation models should be designed, trained, and distilled.
You will develop and evaluate new model architectures, pre-training objectives, data strategies, optimization methods, and teacher–student learning techniques. Your work will explore how capabilities developed in large foundation models can be effectively transferred to smaller, more efficient models without treating distillation as an isolated downstream step.
A major focus of the role will be the co-development of frontier models and efficient models for Apple silicon and on-device intelligence. This includes designing architectures that distill effectively, studying how teacher and student models should be trained together, and developing distillation methods that preserve reasoning, multimodal understanding, instruction following, and other important capabilities under constrained model capacity.
Rather than treating deployment constraints as an afterthought, you will incorporate them into the research process—from early architecture experiments and pre-training through distillation and final model evaluation.
You may thrive in this role if you:
* Want to invent new foundation-model architectures rather than only adapt existing models.
* Enjoy combining scientific ambition with real compute, memory, latency, and energy constraints.
* Believe that small and efficient models can be a frontier research problem, not merely a compression exercise.
* Are comfortable working across model research, data, systems, and hardware boundaries.
* Care about translating research into private, useful, and deeply integrated intelligent experiences.
* Want your work to have both product impact and a presence in the broader research community.
Potential research directions include:
* Novel dense, recurrent, state-space, mixture-of-experts, and hybrid foundation-model architectures.
* Multimodal pre-training across language, images, video, audio, and sensor-derived representations.
* Compute-optimal model and data scaling, including data mixtures, curricula, tokenization, and training objectives.
* Architecture and algorithm co-design for memory-efficient and energy-efficient inference on Apple silicon.
* Offline and on-policy distillation using teacher-generated data, logits, representations, rationales, and other supervision signals.
Minimum qualifications: Hands-on experience designing, implementing, and running large-scale pre-training experiments for large language models.
Experience with LLM pre-training topics such as model architecture, training objectives, data mixtures, tokenization, curricula, scaling, and optimization.
Strong proficiency with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and distributed training systems.
Experience evaluating pre-trained models across language understanding, reasoning, instruction following, or multimodal capabilities.
Strong understanding of transformer-based architectures and current approaches to efficient or scalable foundation-model training.
Master’s degree, or equivalent practical experience in machine learning, computer science, or a related technical field, and a minimum of 6 years relevant experience.
Preferred qualifications: Experience contributing to major foundation-model pre-training efforts or leading architecture experiments that influenced a large training run.
Research contributions in model architecture, scaling laws, multimodal pre-training, optimization, efficient attention, mixture-of-experts, state-space models, or related areas.
Experience with knowledge distillation, including offline or off-policy distillation, on-policy distillation, self-distillation, sequence-level distillation, logic matching, or representation transfer.
Experience designing teacher–student training pipelines or transferring capabilities from large foundation models to smaller models.
Experience with multimodal models spanning language, vision, video, audio, or other sensor modalities.
Understanding of inference efficiency, memory hierarchy, hardware accelerators, or hardware–software co-design.
Strong publication record, influential open-source contributions, or an equivalent record of applied research impact

title: Applied AI Scientist - Multimodal Intelligence
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. Multifaceted, amazing people and inspiring, innovative technologies are the norm here. The same passion for innovation that goes into our products also applies to our practices, strengthening our commitment to leave the world better than we found it. Join us in this truly exciting era of Artificial Intelligence to help deliver the next groundbreaking Apple products & experiences! We are continuously advancing the state of the art in Computer Vision and Machine Learning, touching all aspects of language and multimodal foundation models, from data collection, data curation to modeling, evaluation and deployment. As a member of our dynamic group, you will have the unique and rewarding opportunity to craft upcoming research directions in the field of multimodal foundation models that will inspire future Apple products. Master's or equivalent practical experience, in Computer Science, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, or related technical field.

title: Compute Runtime Software Engineer
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center and Apple platforms — with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements. Beyond the datacenter, we maintain Apple Container, our open source project bringing native container support to macOS desktops.
We're looking to add talented, passionate seasoned domain experts who love hard systems problems and want to build foundational technology used across Apple and the open source community, ready to take ownership of significant technologies.
We build the container runtime technology that Apple's own services and developers depend on. Our systems engineers develop virtualization-based runtimes — using macOS virtualization and VMM solutions like Cloud Hypervisor and sandboxed container solutions — to run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center and Apple platforms, with a relentless focus on privacy, security, and performance. This is a foundational systems team: we work at the level of kernel and container security, image distribution, filesystems, and virtualization. Much of this work is greenfield, solving problems unique to running on Apple's own hardware in the data center, at a scale and with constraints the rest of the industry hasn't had to solve for. Beyond the datacenter, we maintain Apple Container, our open source desktop tooling that lets developers around the world run containers natively on macOS.
We're looking for a domain expert with depth across multiple technical areas, someone used to designing major features and resolving highly complex, ambiguous problems creatively — taking ownership of significant technologies to drive real impact across the organization, ready to take risks, course-correct quickly, and drive ideas from inception to implementation, building a reputation as someone the broader org seeks out for technical direction and standards, and to actively mentor engineers at all levels.
We love open source and collaboration at every level.

Advanced programming language proficiency in C, C++, Swift or Go, with a track record of designing and developing high performance, secured, scalable and reliable systems

title: Manufacturing Design Engineer (MDE) - Watch
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish.

Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
The Apple Manufacturing Design Engineer (MDE) is accountable for driving the development of key mechanical manufacturing processes across Apple’s worldwide supply base. In this highly visible, hands-on role as the expert technical member of the Manufacturing Design Team you will have direct frequent communication and collaboration with Apple Industrial Design, Product Design, Manufacturing Design partners and worldwide suppliers.
Apple MDE’s are extraordinary engineers that provide end to end manufacturing and process solutions for key design features. This includes manufacturing process development and capability (includes incorporating all aspects of equipment, consumables, key parameters, process setup, and qualification), selection and/or design of manufacturing equipment, automation, and strategic R&D.
• Define best-in-class processes to meet all Apple design and operational requirements
• Develop and document processes including all parameters, consumables and secondary operation requirements to meet defined specifications
• Work with Global Supply Managers to define and establish supply chain requirements utilizing selected equipment and manufacturing suppliers
• Provide leadership at manufacturing sites during development and product production ramp, and drive engineering issues to resolution
• Use data to drive process decisions, basic data analysis, DOEs, SPC, etc.
• Identify, research, develop, and qualify premier equipment manufacturers and suppliers
• Define part tolerance and specifications by demonstrating process capability to Product Designers and Industrial Designers
Lead process development/have expertise in one of the process development areas listed below: • CNC machining - Develop all CNC milling and turning processes. Scope appropriate CNC equipment to be used, develop CNC fixtures, implement touch probing, lead the reduction of cycle time, development of advanced cutters and coatings, High Speed Machining implementation, support the programming and optimization of all CNC-related activities at contract manufacturers worldwide. Own yield improvement actions and process change decisions based on statistical process control (SPC) data analysis.
• Surface Finishing - Develop new processes in the area of blasting, tumbling, polishing, wet sanding, lapping, anodizing, and PVD. Ensure that quality and yield requirements are met.
• Glass Processing - Develop all processes for glass scribe/break, grinding, lapping, polishing, chemical strengthening, decoration and functional coatings (with inks, and other thin film deposition techniques etc). Ensure that quality and yield requirements are met.
• Assembly - Develop all assembly processes. Includes incorporating welding, gluing/adhesives, and mechanical fit based processes. Support qualification of equipment at suppliers, including detailed documentation of process parameters. Own yield improvement actions and process change decisions based on statistical process control (SPC) data analysis. Identify automation opportunities and justify automation projects based on automation line efficiency metrics.
• Painting - Develop all paint processes to achieve cosmetic and surface durability requirements. Scope and specify paint equipment, environmental clean room requirements, evaluate and select most appropriate paints and painting parameters to ensure quality and yield requirements are met.
Minimum qualifications: 3+ years of full time mechanical manufacturing experience required
25% domestic and international travel required
BSME or equivalent with MSME or MBA desirable
Preferred qualifications: Demonstrate hands-on mechanical ability
Demonstrate excellent written and verbal interpersonal skills.
Experience with highly cosmetic parts a plus as is experience in a manufacturing environment of consumer electronics or consumer plastic / sheet metal products
Be a self-starter by defining all engineering tasks to meet project objectives and have the ability to quickly learn about new processes with very little information provided

As a member of a fast-paced team, you have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape upcoming products that will delight and inspire millions of people every day.

Strong foundation in computer vision in one or multiple of these areas, including 3D rigid/non-rigid object tracking, multi-view geometry, and visual-inertial odometry (VIO)
Proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch

Experience across both classical 3D computer vision and deep learning

Strong C++ and systems engineering skills, with experience delivering robust, efficient algorithms
Self-motivated with a proven record of prioritization and on-time delivery

title: Senior Manager, Evaluation, Services Special Projects
description:
We are looking for a hands-on Evaluation leader to build and lead a team of applied scientists and machine learning engineers who measure the quality of a new, multi-year Apple initiative. You will join at the start as a key contributor to the evaluation function, working with other eval leaders to establish how the team knows the system is correct, relevant, and trustworthy before and after it ships. You will own specific components of the evaluation plan, including methods, datasets, and automated grading systems that turn product behavior into clear quality signals for engineering and executive leadership.
You will lead a team that designs and runs evaluation for a conversational experience that understands what people ask for, finds and ranks the right results, and allows them to complete tasks. Quality in this product spans several layers: interpreting a request correctly, retrieving and ranking the right results, composing a grounded and accurate response, and executing actions correctly through integrations with external partners. You and your team will be key contributors to the overall evaluation plan for this service and will own the evaluation methods for the layers in your area.
Within your components, you will set the technical direction for large language model (LLM) based autograders and rubrics, including rubric design, evaluation set development, validation, and calibration. You will pair these with logging and instrumentation and online experimentation, working alongside the other eval leaders who own different parts of the plan. You will build the roadmap for your components, translate the broader evaluation strategy into concrete methods and deliverables, and make sure your results turn into measurable quality gains and clear inputs to release decisions.
This is a hands-on role. You will review designs and experiments, stay close to the data, and mentor a team of scientists and engineers while you recruit and grow it. You will partner with engineering, applied machine learning, quality assurance, and program management teams, and you will present quality status, risks, and trade-offs for your areas to senior leadership. The product, its architecture, and its quality bar are still taking shape, so you will operate with significant latitude and help shape what "good" and "shippable" mean as the work evolves.
We're looking for someone with a proven track record in:
Building automated grading systems that scale to large, frequently changing datasets and using them to drive
improvements in models and product features.
Defining metrics and evaluation sets that reflect real user behavior and predict real-world quality.
Turning evaluation findings into action by partnering with engineering and applied machine learning teams to diagnose failures and ship fixes.
Contributing evaluation results to release processes as explicit quality gates.
Growing senior individual contributors and technical leads from within a team, and recruiting strong talent in competitive hiring markets
Minimum qualifications: 6+ years of experience in machine learning, data science, or machine learning evaluation, including 3+ years of
direct people management of scientists or engineers.
Track record of hiring, developing, and leading teams of applied scientists, data scientists, or machine learning
engineers.
Hands-on experience building and deploying LLM-based autograders and rubrics, including rubric design, evaluation
set development, validation, and calibration.
Experience evaluating conversational AI, search, recommendation, or ranking systems, using both offline metrics
and online experimentation.
Strong command of statistics and experimental design, including A/B testing and interpreting noisy metrics.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of influencing engineers and senior leaders
Preferred qualifications: MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent
experience.
Experience evaluating agentic or tool-use systems that take real-world actions, including multi-turn behavior,
planning, and task completion.
Experience with relevance and ranking evaluation, including graded relevance judgments and ranking metrics.
Experience with groundedness and factuality evaluation of generated responses.
Experience with logging infrastructure and instrumentation for AI product quality measurement.
Experience generating and validating synthetic evaluation data.
Experience evaluating systems that integrate with third-party partner APIs.
Experience with privacy-preserving evaluation practices.

title: Senior Security Engineer - Security Assurance Scaling
description:

As a technical lead responsible for the security of Apple's internet-facing services and backend infrastructure, you will be:
Innately curious, listening for nuances and digging into details to understand systems and their weaknesses
Able to identify areas ripe for improvement and establish appropriate security goals
Experienced and comfortable establishing relationships with teams to drive security improvements
Current on new security technologies, vulnerabilities, and methodologies
Able to identify opportunities for automated enforcement and partner with security and platform engineering teams to implement them
Able to use data to drive security review efficiency and prioritize high-value security team engagement
Responsible for security decisions impacting millions of users

Hands-on experience in cloud security engineering with demonstrated expertise in securing at least one major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or AliCloud) in production environments
Experience securing cloud-native applications and workloads, including containerized environments (Kubernetes/EKS/GKE), serverless architectures (Lambda/Cloud Functions), and modern CI/CD pipelines
Experience building, evaluating or directing the use of AI/ML-based security tooling to scale secure design review capacity, demonstrating the ability to recognize and act on automation opportunities
Conversant in at least one programming language such as Python, Java, Go, or Swift
Preferred qualifications: Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience preferred
Experience identifying and prioritizing security enforcement points within infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi) and CI/CD pipelines, and partnering with platform/security engineering teams to embed controls that apply consistently across many teams, rather than relying on manual, one-off reviews

title: Senior Software Engineer (Platform Engineer), G&A Solutions Engineering (GSE)
description:
G&A Solutions Engineering (GSE) is IS&T's dedicated technology partner for Apple's general and administrative functions — including people, finance, facilities, legal, and security.
