The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the da Vinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.

Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.
We provide market-competitive compensation packages, inclusive of base pay + CIP, benefits, and equity. The target pay rate for this position is:
Base salary region 1: $115,500
Base salary region 2: $105,000

title: Assistant General Counsel - Real Estate
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
As an Assistant General Counsel - Real Estate you will provide professional legal advice, counsel, support and guidance to Invenergy’s business operations, focusing primarily on the real estate interests of the company as related to its energy generation and storage portfolio. In addition, you may assist with other general legal matters and various corporate transactions as they arise, and other matters of interest to the company.
This role will be based at either Invenergy's Chicago or Denver offices.
Responsibilities
Providing legal and strategic advice on real estate matters to the Company’s various commercial, operational, and administrative teams.
Managing external counsel on real estate matters related to project development, project financings, and project operations.
Drafting and negotiating various real estate agreements (including leases, easements, options, deeds and other documents).
Drafting and negotiating various key project agreements (including shared facility and co-tenancy agreements, water supply agreements, tax abatement and other host community agreements, and impact mitigation agreements).
Preparing and presenting on general legal and real estate topics.
Minimum Qualifications
JD required.
5-7+ years of relevant experience required, preferably within either a law firm or in a similar context that resulted in real-world experience.
Willing to occasionally travel up to 15% of the time.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.
Preferred Qualifications
Energy industry experience a plus.
Experience with multi-parcel real estate development is preferred.
Proficiency in drafting and reviewing real estate and title curative documents.
Experience in reviewing title work and surveys, and general commercial contract development and negotiation.
Strong organizational, time management, and oral and written communication skills.
High attention to detail.
Ability to prioritize and meet deadlines without sacrificing quality of work product.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability and desire to work effectively in a team environment and with local constituents and decision makers.
The position may require overtime and scheduling to fit the needs of the client.
Base Pay
$180,000.00 - $216,000.00 USD Annual
Bonus: 25% - 40%
The base pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target salary for the position. Invenergy considers a number of factors when determining base pay offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education and skills.
In addition to base pay, the total annual compensation package may also include eligibility to participate in our bonus program(s) which are designed to reward individual and company performance. Your recruiter can share more about bonus eligibility for this position during the hiring process.
Invenergy offers a variety of other benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401k, paid time off, etc.
Invenergy LLC is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, among other things, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, status as a protected veteran, or disability.

title: Senior Associate, Community Engagement
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Job Description
Position Overview
As Senior Associate, Community Affairs, you will lead local outreach and serve as a key relationship contact for county/municipal officials, local taxing bodies, chambers, and Economic Development Organizations where Invenergy has a development or operational presence. An experienced and independently operating professional, the Senior Associate will manage complex community affairs assignments for assigned projects and regions, meaningfully contribute to the design and execution of Invenergy's community relations programs, and help position Invenergy as a good corporate citizen in local communities. This role may also support and mentor junior members of the Community Affairs team.
Responsibilities
Serve as a primary point of contact for local outreach and relationship management with county/municipal officials, local taxing bodies, chambers, and Economic Development Organizations for assigned projects and regions.
Represent projects and Invenergy in meetings with county/municipal officials, local taxing bodies, landowners, and other local and state stakeholders.
Understand and effectively communicate the benefits of operational projects and projects in development to host community members.
Support Invenergy's Development team in navigating county and municipal approval processes required for project development.
Contribute to the development and implementation of structured community relations programs for assigned projects and regions, ensuring alignment with company-wide strategies.
Collaborate with Invenergy's Communications and Impact teams to ensure community relations activities align with company priorities and partnerships.
Communicate effectively with internal and external audiences about Invenergy's presence, industry benefits, and project-specific updates, escalating complex or sensitive matters to the Manager as needed.
Monitor local project opposition; proactively develop relationships with key community members and educate stakeholders to neutralize or mitigate the spread of opposition.
Coordinate with local counties and government groups; maintain close coordination with Invenergy's Government Affairs team to support outreach to local, state, and federal officials.
Summarize and present key statistics about the benefits of operational projects and projects in development to external stakeholders.
Serve as a local contact for key Invenergy stakeholders across assigned regions, maintaining relationship continuity across projects, technologies, and geographies.
Coordinate with Invenergy Asset Management, Operations, and Development teams to identify key stakeholders and advance goals within those departments.
May support the mentorship and development of junior Community Affairs team members (Analysts, Senior Analysts).
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree.
5+ years of experience in fields including infrastructure or real estate development, public affairs, communications, government, politics, law, engineering, environment, sustainability, or related fields.
Demonstrated experience with local political and stakeholder engagement, preferably in rural areas.
Experience working with county/municipal officials, local taxing bodies, chambers, and/or Economic Development Organizations.
Must be able to travel more than 50% of the time; valid driver's license required and willingness to operate personal and/or rented vehicles for travel to project locations, many of which are not accessible by public transit.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.
Preferred Qualifications
Comfortable and experienced in presenting information to a wide variety of audiences and in a wide variety of settings, including one-on-one meetings, public events, and in media settings.
Familiarity with the energy industry, including renewable energy project development, real estate development, or transmission and power engineering.
Strong organizational, networking, leadership, and time management skills.
Ability to write effective, concise reports.
Ability to manage multiple complex tasks simultaneously and in a timely manner, using sound critical thinking and judgment.
Experience mentoring or informally guiding junior team members.
Base Pay
$98,000.00 - $125,000.00 USD Annual
Bonus: 20% - 30%

title: Continuous Improvement Manager
location: Massillon - Salaried, Ohio, United States of America
description:
Lead and support process improvement and business analysis practices throughout the organization. Advise teams in the design and implementation of new technology within the factory setting, such as Connected Factory and Internet-of-Things, to meet production goals. Foster an environment of continuous improvement.
Job Description
The  Continuous Improvement Manager  will provide a full range of productivity services to Operations and direct cost reduction programs for the facility including leading lean events, implementing Kraft Heinz Management System (KHMS) throughout the facility, developing and measuring facility systems and developing and delivering continuous improvement training programs for the facility.  Direction in disciplines of best business practices including, but not limited to, yield improvement, manpower utilization, overhead spend, capital utilization, indirect spend, plant utilization and efficiency, working capital both raw material and finished goods.  This role will act as a coach for the KHMS as well as leading the Site Steering Committee helping to implement KHMS.  This person will work closely with the KHMS Task Force to drive greater utilization of processes and procedures and higher proficiency on the changes impacting employees in the organization such that business results are achieved. This person will provide direct support and coaching to front line managers, supervisors and team leaders as they help their direct reports understand and adopt KHMS.
Key Responsibilities of the Role
Continuous Development of the productivity decks
Generate cost reduction opportunities and implement process improvement to reduce manufacturing costs
Coordinate major initiatives across Supply Chain to insure optimum cost. This coordination will include, but not be limited to, purchasing, distribution, manufacturing, research & development, packaging and engineering
Implement and train MOS & Lean / Six Sigma processes to plant location personnel.
Participate in the QRMP yearly audit and assist in the development of procedures and corrective actions
Assist with the implementation of the QRMP (Quality Risk Management Process) system and operational standards as outlined in the plant accountability list in order to achieve targeted RCR
Share and implement best practice initiatives across Supply Chain
Coordinate the progression of KHMS using TRACC as a tool
Develop and maintain performance (KPI) visuals
Ownership of the Priority One system; responsible to ensure all users are trained and that all projects are current
Develop key performance indicators (KPIs) and tracking system (where needed)
Develop a waste analysis for all lines
Lead and coordinate 5S initiatives plant-wide
Develop and manage the department’s operating budget
Manage and evaluate the Continuous Improvement staff including but not limited to performance management and employee development, etc.
Partner with business leaders on implementation of process improvement (Six Sigma / Lean)
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree is preferred; Preferably in Industrial Engineering or related discipline
3-5 years of operations experience in a manufacturing environment is required
2+ years CI leading CI projects or transformation projects is required
Black/Green Belt Certification preferred
Demonstrated experience overcoming the inevitable problems and obstacles that surface to meet project timelines and cost initiatives
Creativeness and desire to not to be bound by past solutions and to think outside the box in order to drive productivity throughout the organization
Ability to communicate and deal with a range of responsibilities is critical while managing multiple task
Proficiency working in and with well-defined MO systems, ERP systems, productivity tracking systems, AI based systems, and visual workplace tools.
Presentation Skills
Mentoring & coaching skills

title: Field Sales Representative - Chicago
description:
We have multiple openings, with a strong preference for candidates based in the following cities due to customer connectivity: Chicago South (Cook (south side), Will)
Chicago North (Cook (north side), Lake, McHenry)
Job Purpose As an Away From Home (AFH) Field Sales Representative, you will be a key player in driving Kraft Heinz’s market share and profitability within the Chicago territory. This role goes beyond traditional sales—it’s about owning your business, selling solutions, and influencing stakeholders to drive success. We’re looking for a proactive, results-driven individual who can make an impact from day one by building relationships, developing sales strategies, and executing key initiatives. This role offers direct contributions to business growth and valuable sales experience that can pave the way for future career opportunities within Kraft Heinz.    Essential Functions & Responsibilities   ​​Own and lead sales efforts in your assigned territory, driving branded market share and profitability in alignment with Kraft Heinz values.
​Execute the Foodservice Sales Playbook to ensure success in the market.
​Develop and implement profitable sales strategies with local and national distributors while supporting operator needs.
​Build and maintain strong distributor relationships, actively participating in local events and initiatives.
​Drive penetration of priority SKUs, focusing on strategic, branded, and high-margin products.
​Identify and manage a pipeline of high-value sales opportunities, collaborating with Sales Operations, Finance, and Supply teams.
​Lead bottom-up sales planning, crafting data-driven proposals based on customer needs and market insights.
​Own the full sales cycle—from generating interest to securing commitments and closing deals.
​Meet and exceed revenue targets while effectively managing trade budgets and business expenses.
​Execute quarterly and annual sales and marketing priorities, including new product launches and limited-time offers.
​Support the Sales Operations & Planning team by accurately forecasting demand and submitting Volume Submission Forms (VSFs) for new or renewed business.
​ ​   Expected Experience & Required Skills  ​​Bachelor’s degree preferred in business, marketing, sales, or a related field (or equivalent work experience).
​1 to 3 years of sales, customer service, or business development experience, preferably in foodservice, consumer packaged goods (CPG), or a related industry.
​Self-motivated and results-driven with a proactive approach to problem-solving and overcoming challenges.
​Strong analytical skills—ability to interpret sales data, market trends, and financial reports to support business decisions.
​Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to sell and influence both internal and external stakeholders.
​Relationship-building expertise, with the ability to establish and maintain strong partnerships with distributors, operators, and key decision-makers.
​Ability to adapt selling strategies to virtual platforms (MS Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, FaceTime, etc.).
​Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce).
​Ability to lift up to 50 pounds when needed (e.g., delivering customer samples).

The Maintenance Supervisor - 3rd Shift will assist with all maintenance activities to ensure maximum operational potential is realized for the entire plant operation. Improves reliability, maintenance and processing methods to reduce cost and avoid loss of production as a result of equipment malfunction or failure time.

Develops preventative maintenance procedures that are cost effective and increase the operational life of the equipment.

Assist in the development of the system and operational standards and corrective actions.

title: Principal Engineer, R&D - Packaging Materials & Performance
location: Glenview R&D Center, Illinois, United States of America
description:
As the Principal Engineer, Packaging Materials & Performance, you will lead the development and deployment of packaging performance requirements across the Kraft Heinz North America portfolio. The primary purpose of this role is to define the material, package, manufacturing, sustainability, and consumer performance requirements that enable successful packaging development, commercialization, and long-term business performance. These requirements will guide packaging design decisions, supplier alignment, technical validation, and commercialization activities across a diverse portfolio of packaging formats and technologies.
Success in this role requires strong cross-functional collaboration, strategic influence, prioritization, technical problem solving, thoughtful people development, and the ability to lead multiple complex initiatives simultaneously. Working closely with Packaging R&D, Innovation, Platform and Process Packaging, Quality, Operations, Procurement, and external partners, you will establish the technical foundation that ensures packaging systems meet functional, quality, shelf-life, manufacturing, consumer experience, sustainability, and regulatory expectations. Performance specifications are a key output of this work, but the role is fundamentally focused on technical packaging leadership, material performance understanding, and requirement development rather than specification administration. This position also provides leadership for packaging sustainability compliance activities, including support of Extended Producer Responsibility requirements and emerging packaging regulations.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities Lead packaging performance requirements. Define enterprise requirements for packaging materials, package systems, and packaging technologies across the portfolio.
Serve as a technical authority. Provide expertise in barrier properties, mechanical performance, seal integrity, distribution durability, compatibility, machinability, sustainability performance, and consumer use.
Translate needs into measurable criteria. Convert product, consumer, operational, supply chain, sustainability, regulatory, and business needs into clear performance targets and technical acceptance requirements.
Guide material and design decisions. Establish performance targets that inform package development, material selection, supplier engagement, and commercialization choices.
Define and execute validation. Establish testing methods, validation strategies, and acceptance criteria required to demonstrate package performance. Design and oversee packaging validation activities including laboratory testing, pilot plant evaluations, manufacturing trials, distribution testing, and commercial production startup support.
Manage technical risk. Identify, assess, and mitigate risks related to packaging materials, structures, manufacturing processes, and package performance.
Enable commercialization. Build performance verification plans that support concept development, proof of concept, scale-up, launch, and ongoing product support.
Solve complex performance problems. Use scientific and engineering principles, experimental design, and data analysis to investigate failures, close performance gaps, and reduce commercialization risk.
Build organizational capability. Develop tools, training, and coaching that strengthen performance-based packaging development and technical requirement definition.
Build technical capability. Coach and mentor team members in packaging materials, package performance, validation methodologies, commercialization, and technical problem solving. Provide technical leadership and mentorship to cross-functional packaging teams and project stakeholders.
Measure effectiveness. Track outcomes such as commercialization success, reduced rework, improved launch readiness, fewer late-stage changes, and stronger package performance.
Maintain requirement governance. Ensure performance requirements are measurable, technically justified, current, approved, and communicated through effective documentation and change-control practices.
Key Outputs & Deliverables Enterprise packaging performance standards and requirements.
Material and package-system performance criteria for major packaging platforms.
Validation strategies, testing methodologies, and technical acceptance criteria.
Project-ready performance requirements that support innovation, productivity, quality, sustainability, and commercialization objectives.
Technical risk assessments and mitigation plans for packaging systems and material technologies.
Governed performance-requirement documentation that enables clear communication, supplier alignment, and consistent execution.
Training materials, tools, and resources that strengthen packaging development practices across the organization.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
BS/MS/PhD degree in Engineering, Materials, Chemical or Packaging Engineering preferred, or related discipline.
6+ years of experience in packaging R&D, packaging development, materials engineering, commercialization, or related technical leadership roles (consumer goods, food & beverage, pharma or similar preferred).
Packaging-system understanding. Deep understanding of packaging material functionality, package-system interactions, manufacturing processes, and the impact of packaging decisions on product quality, consumer experience, operational performance, and sustainability outcomes. Proven experience establishing technical requirements, performance targets, validation methods, and acceptance criteria for packaging systems. Strong knowledge of packaging manufacturing and converting processes and their effect on package performance and commercialization. Familiarity with sustainable packaging technologies, circularity initiatives, regulatory requirements, and evolving packaging legislation.
Commercialization leadership. Strong experience leading packaging development programs from concept through commercialization. Demonstrated ability to translate consumer, business, manufacturing, supply chain, and product needs into measurable technical requirements.
Experimental design and analysis. Strong understanding of package testing methodologies, Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, data interpretation, and structured technical problem solving.
Learning agility. Strong learning agility and ability to make sound technical decisions in ambiguous, dynamic, and fast-paced environments.
Influence and stakeholder leadership. Proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders, build alignment across a complex network of partners, and lead technical decisions within a matrixed organization.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

The Facilities Technician is responsible for the operation and reliability of all plant systems including high pressure boilers, chillers, cooling towers, air compressors, HVAC systems, Wastewater Treatment (WWT), Ammonia, and facility power supply equipment and processes. The Facilities Technician must possess multi-craft skills (Mechanical and Electrical) and be able to troubleshoot and make repairs to a wide variety of equipment in a safe and efficient manner. This role requires knowledge, competency, professionalism, and safety consciousness to optimize equipment efficiency and longevity while assuring product quality. The Facilities Technician must be able to function with little or no supervision.
This position is responsible for local, state, and federal environmental compliance through internal and external audits and networking with regulators, insurers, and other industry representatives. The Utilities Technician assures adherence to ISO and Mars Wrigley Confectionery Conservation standards. Requirements also include the areas of reliable routine service, timely backlog management and prompt emergency response. The Facilities Technician provides technical knowledge for diagnosing, troubleshooting, repairing and debugging complex utilities issues, computer systems, and/or software. They perform emergency repairs on utilities equipment in a quick, efficient, and safe manner, continuously makes decisions in order of prioritizing tasks to sustain plant operations and production.
Key Responsibilities:
Provide & maintains Steam, Compressed Air, Plant Environmental Conditioning, Fire Protection, Weather protection, and Wastewater Treatment, crucial to plant operation.
Demonstrated expertise in advanced troubleshooting and resolution of system-wide or area-wide, chronic problems in processes and products.
Ensures that the jobs listed in the Daily Shift Checks manual are performed efficiently and in a timely manner. This consists of but is not limited to: Shift checks and logging of equipment operation, chemical testing of boiler and loop systems, assuring safe and efficient operation as well as maintenance of the Boilers and their sub equipment, Chillers and sub equipment, Air compressors and sub equipment, Environmental Air Handler units and sub equipment as well as assist at the WWT if needed.
Ensure adherence to the various operating permits and required inspections mandated by Federal, State, and Local authorities. These include Air, Wastewater, Pressure Vessels, Refrigeration, Storm water and Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plan, by actively following ISO 9000/14001 Standards.
Ensure optimum efficiency of all plant utilities, and wastewater equipment, through preventive/predictive methods. Optimizes preventive maintenance procedures and performs these tasks on assigned area/ systems. Focuses on completion of system generated PM’s and assigned Work Orders. Initiate new PM’s or modify existing PM’s to ensure system optimization.

Works on complex problems.

Job Description:
The fundamental purpose of the Q&FS and Sensory Technologist role is to support factory operations by ensuring quality, food safety, and sensory compliance through the effective implementation and maintenance of quality management systems (QMS), sensory conformance programs, and related processes. This role is responsible for maintaining the plant's quality compliance infrastructure while ensuring finished products and ingredients consistently meet established quality and sensory specifications.
The position requires cross-functional knowledge of factory operations and accountability for implementing quality and sensory-related projects, processes, and programs. Key responsibilities include contributing to QMS compliance by converting recipes into factory systems to meet specifications, maintaining recipe governance for Q&FS-related Statistical Process Control (SPC) parameters, and serving as the site liaison to Supplier Quality Assurance (SQA) for Packaging Holds, coordinating S-CAPA management, communication, and follow-up to support timely resolution of packaging quality issues.
Additionally, the role oversees the sensory evaluation of finished products and ingredients, coordinates daily sensory panels, and supports problem-solving activities related to product quality and sensory conformance.
The role also provides training and guidance to site associates to support on-line sensory programs and works in partnership with BU/Global Sensory Scientists to implement site-specific innovations that strengthen product quality, consistency, and conformance. Through collaboration with cross-functional teams and external partners, this position helps ensure the ongoing effectiveness of quality and sensory systems, supports factory performance, and drives continuous improvement in product quality and compliance.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Qualifications
High school diploma
2-3 years of experience in a manufacturing setting
Strong computer skills
Flexibility to work overtime as needed
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in a science-related discipline or a closely related field.
Internship in quality and food safety in a manufacturing environment or 1-year technical work experience.
Proficient in computer-based applications and digital systems, with experience in SAP, Nexus, Weever, or similar platforms preferred.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Partner with Factory Operations, Supply, Innovation, and Digital teams to collect, analyze, trend, and report material qualification, material performance, and product quality metrics. Identify opportunities for improvement and escalate quality trends and concerns as appropriate.
Serve as the site subject matter expert for translating formulas and recipes into factory operating systems, including SAP Bill of Materials (BOM) creation, Weever management, and change control processes to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Lead site governance and management of Statistical Process Control (SPC) for finished product specifications and Key Quality Attributes. Monitor and optimize quality-related SPC processes, support system enhancements, and ensure alignment with Supply requirements.
Support material quality management and incident resolution for raw and packaging materials. Serve as the site liaison to Supplier Quality Assurance (SQA) for Packaging Holds, coordinating communication, S-CAPA activities, and follow-up to drive timely resolution.
Execute site sensory conformance requirements through the evaluation and analysis of raw materials, in-process materials, and finished products. Identify, investigate, and resolve sensory-related issues; escalate non-conformances; and recommend appropriate ingredient and finished product disposition.
Lead site-based Conformance and Online Sensory Programs, including associate recruitment, training, calibration, and program execution. Ensure compliance with established best practices and minimum program requirements while maintaining accurate sensory performance records.
Partner with BU/Global Sensory Scientists to implement site-specific innovations and strengthen sensory conformance. Actively participate in the Sensory Quality Community of Practice (COP) to share best practices, align ways of working, and drive continuous improvement across MW manufacturing sites.
Coach, train, and guide site associates to strengthen technical capabilities and competencies across Quality, Technical Services, and Innovation. Support sensory quality assessments and training for co-manufacturing operations.

title: Shift Manager (Nights)
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
The Shift Manager is a front-line operations leader responsible for improving Quality, Human Safety, and Product Cost Efficiency while engaging and developing talent. This role leads teams of 25-30 production associates, ensuring operational targets are met. The Shift Manager focuses on safety, quality, performance management, continuous improvement, and associate development for their assigned area. They collaborate with the 24-hour Area Leadership Team to implement continuous improvement strategies and Supply Excellence initiatives. This leader is also responsible for building and managing an effective team, ensuring proper training, and enforcing policies.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Production Efficiency: Lead multi-line teams to efficiently convert materials into quality products in a safe, sanitary manner, meeting product design specifications.
Change Management: Implement and recommend changes in methods, equipment, or systems to achieve operational goals using a Continuous Improvement mindset.
Supply Excellence (SE): Lead or support SE Pillars, including Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs), ensuring accuracy in reliability data collection.
Nature’s Bakery Operating System: Advocate for and support the site's Daily Management System, coaching teams in the Value Stream Operating System.
Area Ownership: Collaborate with the Area Leadership Team to create and execute a reliability strategy for your area.
Coaching: Develop operators’ functional and leadership skills while driving accountability in safety, quality, and team engagement.
Operations Coordination: Manage materials, staffing, and resources to support line operations and changeovers.
Standards Implementation: Ensure standards are communicated, reinforced, and adhered to through coaching and accountability.
Safety and Quality: Drive a strong focus on safety and food safety, ensuring the ongoing production of safe, defect-free products. HACCP proficiency is required.
Associate Development: Manage associate relations, recruitment, training, and development, fostering a high-engagement team environment.
Performance Management: Set performance goals, measure progress, and take corrective action as needed.
Troubleshooting: Lead preventive maintenance and equipment troubleshooting efforts to achieve desired performance.
Escalations: Identify risks and resolve escalated issues on-shift, assigning resources as necessary.
Communication and Engagement: Ensure open communication and foster an environment of high associate engagement.
Technological Advancement: Identify opportunities for technological improvements to enhance line performance.
Strategy Implementation: Help implement strategies to drive near-term operational improvements.
Recruitment and Onboarding: Partner with Talent Acquisition to recruit, select, and onboard associates for operational roles.
EXPERIENCE
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience (4+ years in a technical manufacturing continuous improvement environment with a High School Diploma).
Prior experience leading manufacturing teams for 4+ years with high preference for direct report responsibility leading larger production teams
Demonstrated leadership experience, preferably with direct people management.
Knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and plant operations.
Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate across all functions.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, etc.)
Experience with plant sanitation practices and OSHA safety standards or certifications.
HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
Ability to deliver performance feedback and hold associates accountable to business objectives.

Medical, dental, and vision insurance offered for eligible employees

description:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role

As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective.

In this role, you will:

 - Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs.

 - Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

 - Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights.

 - Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions.

 - Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners.

 - Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes.

 - Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact.

 - Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs.

 - Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty.

 - Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options.

 - Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions.

 - Turn incident lessons into practical improvements to readiness, playbooks, detection coverage, and response tooling.

title: Director, Mechanical Sourcing
description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
At Oura, our mission is to empower people to live healthier, longer. With our award-winning Oura Ring and app, we help millions of people understand their sleep, activity, and readiness so they can live healthier, more balanced lives.
We are looking for a Director, Global Mechanical Sourcing to lead the strategy, execution, and development of Oura’s global mechanical sourcing organization. This leader will own mechanical sourcing across current and future hardware programs, with global responsibility spanning the established Finland and US teams and broader regional supplier partnerships.
This is an established function with strong leaders and processes already in place. The Director will align mechanical sourcing strategy across team based in the US, Finland, and Asia; connect priorities across the portfolio; improve decision-making; and be accountable for the function’s results as Oura grows - building on what is working while addressing the gaps that require a stronger global approach.
The Director will lead through existing leaders and teams, develop sourcing talent, strengthen the operating model, and raise the bar for analytical standards and commercial discipline. The role will work closely with Product, Industrial Design, Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Program Management, Finance, Legal, Logistics, and senior leadership.
This role is for a leader who can set direction, stay close enough to the details to know what is really happening, lean in to contribute directly as necessary, and make decisions when the information is incomplete. The work will require resilience with suppliers, direct communication, and good judgment. The right leader will manage effectively up and down, stay accountable for outcomes, and invest deeply in the growth of their direct reports. They will hold themselves and the team to a high standard of integrity, collaboration, and follow-through.
This is a hybrid role requiring someone to work 2-3 days a week out of our San Francisco office.
What You Will Do
Set the global mechanical sourcing strategy
Define and execute a multi-year global mechanical sourcing strategy aligned to Oura’s product roadmap, margin goals, quality standards, launch plans, resilience requirements, and manufacturing footprint.
Set supplier architecture across regions, technologies, and production stages, including preferred suppliers, second sources, geographic diversification, and capability-development priorities.
Create or iterate category strategies for key mechanical commodities such as CNC, injection molding, stamping, MIM, die casting, surface finishing, coatings, structural components, die cuts, softgoods, and related packaging categories where applicable.
Translate market conditions, technology developments, supplier capacity, geopolitical exposure, and cost drivers into clear recommendations for senior leadership.
Build a global mechanical sourcing roadmap that aligns priorities, supplier architecture, and tradeoffs across regions, building on existing strategies and processes while closing the observed gaps.
Lead and develop the global team
Lead the global mechanical sourcing organization through its existing leaders, aligning regional priorities and setting clear outcomes and decision rights across regions, commodities, programs, and supplier relationships.
Set a high bar for performance, decision quality, communication, and follow-through while creating an environment where people can do their best work.
Build and execute development plans for managers and individual contributors, including coaching, feedback, career paths, succession planning, and opportunities for expanded scope.
Assess organizational capability and capacity against Oura’s product roadmap; hire, structure, and develop the team as the business grows.
Set a common operating cadence with consistent mechanisms for strategy reviews, supplier performance, risk escalation, negotiation planning, and executive updates.
Build a strong working culture across geographies, challenge the status quo with respect, and help the team stay focused when the work gets difficult.
Bring analytical rigor to cost and value decisions
Establish a fact base for mechanical cost and value decisions, including should-cost models, supplier benchmarks, cost-driver analysis, total-cost-of-ownership analysis, and scenario planning.
Create visibility into mechanical cost trajectories across the product lifecycle and partner with Finance and Product Cost teams to connect sourcing actions to gross margin and business plans.
Use data to evaluate supplier proposals, manufacturing alternatives, volume assumptions, tooling and NRE, yield, labor, material, freight, payment terms, and other total-cost drivers.
Standardize scorecards and review mechanisms that make supplier performance, cost, quality, delivery, capacity, responsiveness, and risk visible to the right stakeholders.
Make sure recommendations are grounded in clear assumptions, evidence, and a realistic path to execution.
Build vendor strategy and supplier performance
Own supplier selection and portfolio decisions for mechanical components and assemblies across NPI and sustaining programs.
Develop executive-level relationships with strategic suppliers and contract manufacturing partners across North America, Europe, and Asia.
Lead supplier capability assessments, onboarding, qualification, business reviews, corrective-action plans, and long-term partner development.
Set expectations for supplier performance, capacity planning, quality, responsiveness, transparency, and continuous improvement.
Build supply continuity plans that address concentration, geographic risk, capacity constraints, financial health, tooling ownership, materials, and contingency options.
Partner with Engineering and suppliers on DFM, design-for-cost, manufacturing capability, process innovation, and tradeoffs that improve product performance and production readiness.
Lead complex negotiations
Lead or oversee high-impact negotiations covering unit cost, tooling and NRE, capacity commitments, lead times, payment terms, minimum order quantities, price-adjustment mechanisms, warranty, E&O and liability, intellectual property, and other commercial terms.
Prepare negotiation strategies grounded in should-cost analysis, supplier economics, market alternatives, business priorities, and a clear understanding of Oura’s negotiating position and constraints.
Represent Oura credibly with supplier executives and align internal stakeholders before entering critical commercial discussions.
Secure outcomes that support Oura’s business goals, including cost competitiveness, supply assurance, investment, flexibility, quality, and launch execution.
Ensure agreements and commitments are documented, governed, and translated into measurable supplier actions.
Own execution across the hardware lifecycle
Be accountable for operational and commercial outcomes across the mechanical portfolio, including NPI, and ensure escalations are resolved through the right leaders.
Stay close to critical supplier, build-readiness, capacity, quality, cost, and commercial issues. Personally lean in when impact or urgency calls for it, and otherwise drive decisions to closure through the accountable leaders.
Ensure sourcing strategy is integrated into design reviews, supplier selection, development builds, manufacturing readiness, capacity planning, and launch decisions.
Work with Manufacturing, Quality, Logistics, Finance, and Legal to resolve cross-functional issues and make tradeoffs that protect cost, quality, schedule, resilience, customer experience, and brand.
Improve sourcing processes, templates, systems, and governance so the team can move with speed while maintaining decision quality and control.
Provide concise, fact-based updates to senior leadership on strategy, cost, risk, supplier performance, decisions, and support needed.
Requirements
We would love to have you on our team if you have:
12+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, supply chain, operations, manufacturing, or a related field, with significant experience in mechanical components and assemblies.
Experience leading global sourcing teams across multiple regions, including managing effectively through leaders, developing direct reports, and building strong, accountable teams.
Deep experience with mechanical manufacturing processes such as CNC, injection molding, stamping, MIM, die casting, surface finishing, adhesives, die cuts, softgoods, or related technologies.
Experience in consumer electronics, wearables, medical devices, or another product business with complex, miniaturized hardware.
Experience owning category strategy, supplier architecture, and day-to-day supplier execution.
Strong analytical skills, including should-cost modeling, cost-driver analysis, supplier benchmarking, financial analysis, scenario planning, and total-cost-of-ownership evaluation.
A proven record of leading complex negotiations with supplier and contract manufacturing executives across cost, tooling, capacity, quality, liability, and long-term commercial terms.
Experience supporting multiple concurrent NPI programs through development, ramp, mass production, and sustaining, with a track record of personally engaging in critical operating issues when the business needs it.
Strong understanding of DFM, supplier qualification, manufacturing readiness, quality systems, supply continuity planning, and the operational and commercial escalation paths needed to keep NPI programs moving.
Executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to turn complex data and tradeoffs into clear recommendations and decisions.
The judgment to balance cost, quality, schedule, resilience, innovation, customer experience, and business value.
The ability to operate effectively across cultures, time zones, and functions in a fast-moving, sometimes ambiguous environment.
A leadership style that is direct, accountable, collaborative, and grounded in high standards for themselves and the people they lead.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally approximately 25–30% as needed.
Preferred qualifications
Experience leading mechanical sourcing for wearables, smart devices, or other high-volume consumer hardware.
Experience working across both European and US-based engineering, sourcing, and supplier organizations.
Experience with packaging, finishing, coatings, adhesives, softgoods, or other adjacent mechanical categories.
Experience with supplier development, value engineering, design-to-cost, or manufacturing process innovation.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field. A master’s degree is a plus.
This is a hybrid role
The candidate should be based in the San Francisco Bay Area and able to come into the office regularly. This role will work closely with colleagues in Finland and other global locations.

description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Role Summary Rivian is on a mission to build the future of sustainable mobility, and our commercial operations are where that mission meets our customers. Our Enterprise Digital team designs the tools behind sales, fulfillment and service: the systems our teams use every day to sell vehicles, deliver them and keep them on the road. Designing enterprise tools at Rivian isn’t about back-office forms. It’s about software that people across retail, delivery and service depend on to do their jobs well, where clarity and speed directly shape the customer experience. You’ll take complex business processes and turn them into simple, intuitive tools. We’re looking for someone who is a natural systems thinker and a strong communicator. Our team is defined by our ability to ask good questions, get comfortable with complicated business functions, reframe problems simply and bring others along. Responsibilities Problem Framing & Strategy: Work with product, engineering and leaders in sales, fulfillment and service to find the real bottlenecks, help shape roadmaps and write clear design briefs with measurable goals. Field Research: Spend time in retail spaces, delivery centers and service centers to see how work actually happens, talk with the people doing it, and understand the friction and edge cases they face. Systems Thinking: Map complex business processes, policies and data, and turn them into clear user flows, information architecture and interfaces that reduce effort and error. Preferred:

title: Business SOX Compliance Manager
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara is looking for an experienced manager to lead SOX business process compliance and help keep the trust in our financial reporting as strong as the business we’re building. As part of our SOX Compliance team, you’ll help oversee and strengthen Samsara’s global control environment, protecting the accuracy of our financial reporting and keeping us compliant as we scale. You’ll partner closely with IT and business process owners to design and implement controls, spot gaps early, and drive remediation to the finish line. We’re looking for someone who takes real ownership. You bring deep, hands-on SOX expertise, a track record of delivering projects reliably, and the confidence to run with complex work independently. If you take pride in being the person others count on to get it done right, we’d love to meet you.
This is a remote position open to candidates based in the US  except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.
In this role, you will:
Develop, lead, and execute periodic financial risk assessments, materiality calculations, and scoping of the SOX program
Develop and deliver training to SOX control owners, including process documentation, testing methodology, management review controls, and controls over Information Produced by the Entity (IPE).
Conduct walkthroughs across all business process areas and work with business process owners to ensure timely review and updates to the control documentation
Collaborate cross functionally to design leading edge practices with a financial compliance mindset across several complex business process areas.
Monitor and assess emerging financial reporting risks with the growth and evolution of the business and develop plans to implement appropriate controls to timely address these emerging risks
Ownership of control deficiency evaluation, aggregation analysis as well as development and execution of related remediation plans.
Help drive the SOX AI transformation strategy by identifying high-value opportunities, implementing AI-enabled solutions, and driving adoption and new ways of working across the global SOX organization.
Provide reporting to business leaders on program status, health, and effectiveness of the business process control environment
Collaborate and align with the company’s external audit and internal audit around financial reporting risks, design of ICFR monitoring systems,and SOX program approach
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Minimum requirements for the role:
7+ years of SOX 404 / ICFR experience at a Big Four (internal or external audit) or combination of Big Four and public company experience
Hands-on experience with risk assessment, scoping, walkthroughs, control design, and deficiency evaluation
Strong knowledge of order to cash, procure to pay, financial close and reporting controls
Ability to identify, assess  and explain risks and control gaps clearly to executives and other non-technical audiences
Working knowledge of COSO 2013, PCAOB AS 2201, and SEC ICFR guidance, including management review controls and IPE
Bachelor's in accounting or finance (CPA and/or CIA preferred)
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience with financial systems such as Netsuite, Salesforce, Workday and Xactly
Experience using automation or AI tools to make compliance work faster, more reliable, and SOX compliant
Experience working closely with Internal Audit and External Auditors
Strong communication skills, including presenting to and influencing senior business leaders
Demonstrated success managing worksteams/project independently

We’re looking for an Electrical Engineer co-op to join our team. In the day-to-day, you will be responsible for working on the EE aspects of the design of products based on thorough feasibility, design, and cost studies encompassing key component selection, thermals, antenna, etc. We have a tremendous amount of telemetry and access to customers that help guide our design process. You will work directly with our customers to ensure we lead the industry with our product design. We run a collaborative process working closely with Product Management, PD, FW, EPM, NPI, and Hardware leadership to make excellent tradeoffs and choices. Throughout this process, you’ll share your expertise with other engineers. The US and Taiwan EE teams are supported by the Supply Chain team, laboratories, JDM design resources, and a growing supply base. You will work closely with these internal and external partners to achieve our objectives.
This role will be held at our San Francisco office. Co-ops are required to be in the office Tuesdays to Thursdays and remote work days on Mondays and Fridays. As part of the co-op program, we do provide relocation and housing support for the duration of the co-op. We’re hiring Engineering Managers across multiple verticals. The nice thing about growing 30%+ at ~$2.1B ARR is that we need great engineering leaders everywhere, and we have the room to shape the team around the right person. You lead like a founder. We give you the platform to do it at scale.
About the role:
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We’re still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we’re hiring the leaders who will build the teams that build what comes next.
We’re at ~$2.1B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.
We’re looking for Engineering Managers who want to define what ships next by building and leading great teams. You’ll manage engineers across platform and product, and we’re open to shaping team scope around the right person’s strengths and interests. That window won’t stay open long.
This role is remote and open to candidates residing in the US or Canada. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world. The software your team builds will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn’t metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.
You want to build, not maintain. Samsara is in full growth mode. Your team will build new systems from scratch, not babysit old ones. You’d own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.
You want to work where AI meets the physical world. Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.
You believe customers are more than a number. Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You and your team will participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.
You believe great teams are the real product. You get energy from hiring exceptional people, growing them, and creating the conditions for them to do the best work of their careers. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn’t tooling or process. It’s ambition, and your job is to unlock it.
In this role, you will:
Lead and grow a team of engineers: hire top talent, coach and develop individuals, manage performance, and build a culture of ownership, quality, and velocity.
Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.
Define and drive technical strategy and roadmap for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.
Guide your team to design and ship full-stack features end to end, delivering AI-powered products that solve real operational problems across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile.
Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans, staffing, and measurable outcomes.
Oversee the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators, and stay close enough to the technical work to guide architecture and make sound tradeoffs.
Raise the bar across engineering through design reviews, hiring standards, mentorship of senior engineers and future leaders, and by setting the standard for quality, velocity, and craft.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.
Minimum requirements for the role:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.
3+ years of experience directly managing software engineers, including hiring, performance management, and career development.
Strong technical fundamentals across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile), enough to guide architecture, review designs, and earn your team’s respect.
Familiarity with modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).
Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.
Experience building or leading teams that build AI-powered or data-driven products. You don’t need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.
Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders, including executives.
A track record of building: zero-to-one products, teams and systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that’s LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.
Experience leading teams through AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply output and accelerate delivery.
Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.
A proven track record of managing and developing senior engineers, building managers-of-managers, and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.
Experience scaling teams through fast growth, including building hiring pipelines and onboarding.

The Commercial team is a high-velocity sales team focused on acquiring new, under-penetrated mid-market customers. As an Account Executive on the Commercial Hunter sales team, you’ll be responsible for sourcing and closing net new business, executing outbound sales strategies, and running end-to-end sales cycles to bring new customers onto Stripe. You’ll play a critical role in expanding Stripe’s reach by identifying high-potential prospects and converting them into long-term users of our platform.
